narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
intent: To illustrate the partisan divide in support for replacing the Electoral College, demonstrating that Democrats are the primary proponents of a popular vote.

units.meaning: The value series rises from 44 in 2000 to a peak of 52 in 2010, then falls to 23 in 2020.

basis.note: start value; Republicans have identical value
peak value; Republicans have identical value
end value; Republicans have identical value

accepted_routes: Value starts at 44 in 2000, peaks at 52 in 2010, and ends at 23 in 2020.
The series rises from 44 to 52, then declines to 23 by 2020.
After a rise through 2010, the value falls sharply to its lowest point in 2020.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The animated data marks must move upward from 2000 to 2010 and downward to 2020 for both parties.
units.temporal_anchor: Should be conveyed during the data animation; not explicitly stated in the narration.
units.reviewer_question: Is the full rise-then-fall trend required, or is only the partisan comparison required by the intent?

units.meaning: The maximum value in the table is 52 at 2010.

basis.note: maximum value in table; Republicans have identical value

accepted_routes: The highest value shown is 52 in 2010.
The series reaches its maximum of 52 at 2010.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 2010 mark must be shown as the highest point on the value series.
units.reviewer_question: Is the peak value required, or is the overall trend sufficient?

units.meaning: The largest drop is from 52 in 2010 to 25 in 2015, a decrease of 27 in the table's value.

basis.note: start of largest drop; Republicans have identical value
end of largest drop; Republicans have identical value

accepted_routes: The value falls by 27 from 2010 to 2015.
Between 2010 and 2015, the value drops from 52 to 25.
The sharpest decline is from 52 at 2010 to 25 at 2015.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must show a steep decline between the 2010 peak and the 2015 value.
units.temporal_anchor: During the decline phase of the animation.
units.reviewer_question: Is the largest single drop required, or is the full trend enough?

units.meaning: The minimum value in the table is 23 at 2020.

basis.note: minimum value in table; Republicans have identical value

accepted_routes: By 2020 the value has fallen to 23, the lowest in the table.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 2020 mark must be shown as the lowest point on the value series.
units.reviewer_question: Is the endpoint minimum required, or is the change from peak sufficient?

units.meaning: Democrats and Republicans have identical values at every year in the table; no partisan gap is shown in the provided data.
accepted_routes: Democrats and Republicans have the same values at every year in the table.
The two party series are identical, so there is no partisan gap.
The table shows no difference between Democrats and Republicans.
Both parties overlap exactly in the data.
units.visual_evidence_rule: If both parties are visualized, their data marks must coincide at each year; the video must not depict one party as higher.
units.temporal_anchor: The narration's second sentence about Democrats leading the charge; the data does not support a difference.
units.reviewer_question: Should the video follow the intent's partisan-divide claim even though the table's values are identical for both parties?

optional_valid: Exact intermediate values (e.g., 46.6087 at x_px 725) are optional if the overall trend and endpoints are conveyed.
Using relative_value instead of value for a normalized trend shape is optional, but it must be described relatively, not as a percentage.
Highlighting the 2015 value of 25 as an intermediate low is optional.
unsupported_to_avoid: Democrats have higher support than Republicans.
Democrats are the primary proponents as a measured data difference.
Any percentage, e.g., 44% or 23%, because the unit column is blank.
Causal claims that Electoral College disadvantage causes Democrats to lead the charge.
Republican presidents winning the popular vote or Electoral College outcomes.
notes: The table's value column has no unit and both entities are identical across all rows; the intent's partisan divide is not supported by the provided data. The core data story is a rise from 44 in 2000 to 52 in 2010, then a fall to 23 in 2020.
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
